text: Proposition one asks whether California should borrow money
for housing.
This measure authorizes eleven point two five billion
dollars: ten billion for housing programs, and one
point two five billion for veterans’ home loans.
The General Fund would repay the housing portion
at about five hundred to six hundred million
dollars a year for roughly twenty-five years.
Veterans’ loan payments would repay their separate bond
portion.
A voter might support financing affordable homes sooner
rather than waiting for enough money in annual
budgets.
Interest adds expense, and future repayments compete with
other services.
Yes authorizes this borrowing;
no rejects this bond, while existing housing programs
continue.
